items.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries no rival boundary at all -- it rejects two unit_type labels -- so this six-verse span ships without engagement of any rival cut, including one its own prose points at.
items.auditor_grounds: The field rejects forcing the span into wasf_poem or narrative_sequence as a worse fit than lyric_address, and says the span is argued into lyric_address by the closest-fit operative category with the deviation disclosed below. That is a unit_type justification, and the book's operative-category law routes exactly that disclosure to device_notes, where this row already carries it -- so the rival-boundary slot is spent on a duplicate. A rival cut was available from the row's own bytes: MT 3:7-3:10 carry no first- or second-person address form at all (verified -- every suffix across those four verses is third-person), and MT 3:11 then opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte), two 2fp imperatives plus the book's only daughters-of-Zion vocative (sweep: 1 verse), which under the book's voice policy is tier-1 voice-shift evidence standing exactly at the 3:10|3:11 junction. The row's own device_notes concedes the point by saying the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, and separately discloses a span-internal setumah at MT 3:8 (single-witness tier-3, correctly non-driving) at the other candidate joint. I am NOT concluding that the shipped span is wrong -- the maximal-run rule and the processional coherence support holding MT 3:6-3:11 whole -- only that the strongest available rival is unengaged, which is a warrant gap on a medium_low row. Not alone load-bearing: both outer edges stand on byte-verified tier-1 anchors. Noted inside the same sentence and folded into this finding rather than scored separately: the phrase closest-fit operative category imports governance vocabulary into row prose.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unit_type sentence with an actual rival-cut engagement -- reject, or accept and re-span, the 3:10|3:11 cut at the daughters-of-Zion vocative onset, quoting the pointed splice at oshb:Song.3.11 with its tier -- and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already stands in device_notes. Any resulting respan is an adjudication question, not this review's proposal.
items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium (rival-engagement: a defective warrant at an internal tier-1 joint, not alone load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The finding's factual ground holds. Every suffix and verb form across oshb:Song.3.6-Song.3.10 is third person: 3fs עֹלָה֙ and מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier); 3ms/3fs מִטָּתוֹ֙ ... לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier); 3mp/3ms כֻּלָּם֙ ... חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל יְרֵכ֔וֹ (oshb:Song.3.8, byte tier); עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier); עַמּוּדָיו֙ ... רְפִידָת֣וֹ ... מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ ... תּוֹכוֹ֙ (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier). A scan of the pointed bytes of those five verses finds no final-kaf suffix (the only final-kaf tokens are the noun הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:9 and בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:11), no 1cs -ti perfect, no 1cp -nu form and no independent first- or second-person pronoun; the yod-final tokens are construct plurals (form claims argued from the pointed bytes plus the WEB rendering; no morphology layer is staged). Then oshb:Song.3.11 opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte tier; WEB “Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see” web:Song.3.11): two feminine-plural imperatives plus the daughters-of-Zion vocative, which the book's voice policy lists by name among its tier-1 formula anchors (adjacent-pair sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse, MT 3:11; the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair sweeps 7 verses at skeleton tier only because it catches the from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם at oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier, which is not an address). So a tier-1-marked rival cut stands at the 3:10|3:11 joint exactly as the finding says. (2) BOTH SIDES of that rival seam weighed from bytes. The preceding verse closes תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier) with no parashah seg at MT 3:10 (the WLC inventory's segs in this span sit at MT 3:8 and MT 3:11, single-witness, tier-3; absence is never counterevidence). The following verse continues the same referent after its summons: בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ... לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ ... וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) carries on the 3ms suffix chain of MT 3:9-3:10 and the Shelomo chain שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) (Shelomo-skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, one of them the homograph at MT 1:7; 3 of the 8 inside this span). The governing rule that decides: the hybrid granularity permits a cut at a tier-1 marker but does not compel one, and the summons-to-view reads as the unit's own close because its object is the king the description has been building (tier-2 referential continuity, used here only to reject a cut, never to drive a seam), corroborated at tier 3 by the setumah standing AT MT 3:11 rather than at MT 3:10 (single witness). The shipped span is therefore defensible and I propose no respan. (3) The shipped row's defect is real. Its strongest_rejected_alternative rejects two unit_type labels (wasf_poem, narrative_sequence) and names no rival cut; the operative-category law routes exactly that deviation disclosure to device_notes, where the row already carries it, so the rival slot is spent on a duplicate. The row's only engagement of the 3:10|3:11 joint is the device_notes concession that the addressee shift surfaces at the closing imperative, while boundary_rationale treats a marker of the book's own tier-1 class as a unit-internal close without saying why it does not open a unit. That is an unargued warrant at the one internal joint where the book's law demands engagement: a defective warrant, medium. Not high, because both outer seams stand on tier-1 anchors weighed from both sides: front, the full adjuration הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Song.3.5, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:5, single-witness tier-3) closes the seek-find episode and מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier; collates byte against oshb:Song.8.5 as well; ascent-formula sweep, skeleton tier: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5; bare mi-zot interrogative 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) opens a fresh 3fs question; rear, MT 3:11 closes on שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:11, single-witness tier-3) and הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.4.1, byte tier) opens the his-word address, coherent with the adjacent shipped rows Song.3.5-Song.3.5 and Song.4.1-Song.4.7, which argue those same seams from their own sides. Not low: this is not a mechanical or register slip but the missing half of the row's own warrant for a six-verse span (the register bleed the auditor folded in, the governance phrase closest-fit operative category inside row prose, is a genuine low-severity component and moves the severity neither way). (4) Repair proposal tested as adversarially as the row: the field repair is byte-sound and is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with this qualification: the replacement sentence should REJECT the 3:10|3:11 cut on the grounds in (2) (the 3ms referential chain and the Shelomo chain binding MT 3:11 to MT 3:9-3:10; the setumah at MT 3:11 disclosed single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only), quoting the pointed onset splice of oshb:Song.3.11 with its byte tier, and leave the deviation disclosure in device_notes; the accept-and-respan branch is not supported by these bytes and is not proposed. Non-span item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of every seam in play were weighed from bytes.

items.claim: The Shulammite uniqueness citation blends two count objects: the in-verse occurrence digit it reports is false for the byte-swept token it names.
items.auditor_grounds: The row writes the epithet citation as a single byte-tier object with two digits - 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse. Re-swept with the object named: the byte-tier token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13) returns 1 verse and 1 token occurrence book-wide, not 2. The verse's second epithet token is בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a bet-prefixed form that is a different string at byte tier AND at skeleton tier, and it byte-sweeps to 1 verse / 1 token of its own. The 2-occurrence digit is true only for the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton, which sweeps to 1 verse and 2 token occurrences. neighbour_prev_post_repair.device_notes: The shalhevet-yah pair (MT 8:6) is a classic crux (OSHB exegesis note, single-witness apparatus): the construal (intensive 'mighty flame' versus divine element) is held, not decided, and the one-word/divided-token fact is disclosed on this citation; this is the Yah-form surface (sweep: 1 verse) in a book carrying zero plain YHWH/Elohim citations (sweep: 0 of 117 verses, byte-swept). The mi-zot formula at MT 8:5 is the ascent-run member (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5), a distinct object from the bare mi-zot interrogative (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) — the two counts are never blended. The span opens on this ascent formula and a 1cs/2ms address chain before it reaches the aphoristic peak at MT 8:6, a deviation from the exemplar epigram shape retained under the same category because no tier-1 marker separates the opening question and address from the peak that follows.

neighbour_next_post_repair.boundary_rationale: Her retort to the brothers opens on the 1cs pronoun אֲנִ֣י (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), which fixes the speaker as singular against the 1cp נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר of the brothers' oshb:Song.8.9 (byte tier), and the gender-marked forms carrying the attribution itself sit later in the same verse: the feminine-singular participle כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) 'found as one who finds peace', and the 3ms suffix בְעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) locating the other party as a man. WEB: “I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.” (web:Song.8.10). Her own answer, אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה 'I am a wall', answers their wall/door hypothetical with a concrete self-claim rather than a general maxim, and וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת answers their וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ from oshb:Song.8.8 (both byte tier).
